When he had heard of her departure so soon,
He went to his chamber where she used to sit;
And there in a corner lay the old lute hung.

"The lute I left behind me at home! " said he,
"And shall be told that it was my brother brought!"
She caught him by the shoulder, while he stood there dumb,
And laughed and cried, "It is my poor heart's delight."

But he would not listen, though she begged him again,--
His mind was fixed upon the coming pain.

text:
A Maiden In The Springtime

The maiden in the springtime
Weaves a scarf with her hair,
And from it she selects two threads to weave into a web of light,
Then lays them down as dew upon the grass,
That is to be their home until they are plucked by night,
So that the little birds may build there.

We're told they ought to be paid from the gate,
And when they make a touchdown I feel like praying for fate.

But when they play with their backs against the wall,
When there's no more time out on which to call,
Then we have faith in our soul team,
For we all pull together as One For All!

text: We are back in a world we knew only from history books--a medieval England on the eve of the Black Death (1348), which was to kill 20 million people across Europe, about half the population. The plague was caused by fleas carried by rats, but there were few rat catchers then. No doctors understood what was happening. They had no concept of germs and disease. As they did now, they resorted to fumigation and quarantines as remedies against unknown diseases. But they had no means of stopping them spreading. So this is how you get into such terror.
